listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
A formal letter is for people you don't know well, officials, or businesses.
FORMAT:
1. YOUR ADDRESS (top right)
2. DATE
3. RECIPIENT'S ADDRESS (left)
4. GREETING: Dear Mr./Mrs./Ms. [Name], or Dear Sir/Madam,
5. OPENING: I am writing to...
6. BODY: Your request/information
7. CLOSING: Thank you for your time. / I look forward to your reply.
8. SIGN-OFF: Yours sincerely, (if you know name) / Yours faithfully, (if you don't)
9. YOUR NAME
TONE:
- NO contractions: I am, do not, cannot
- Polite language: May I, Could you, Would you
- Formal vocabulary: request, regarding, appreciate
- Professional sentences
Example opening:
"Dear Mr. Principal,
I am writing to request permission to organize a school clean-up day."
dictation: A formal letter is for people you don't know well, officials, or businesses.

MATH/SCIENCE Extension Notes (teacher only):

Topic: Order of Operations (PEMDAS)

Math Reading Input (100 words):
Which Comes First?
When we have many operations, which one do we do FIRST?
We use PEMDAS:
P - Parentheses (brackets) first
E - Exponents (powers)
M - Multiplication } left to right
D - Division     }
A - Addition     } left to right
S - Subtraction  }
Example: 2 + 3 ×

Word Problem approach: Guide students step by step.
Answer:
